transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Since we're six weeks out from the planned voice-authentication rollout at our U.S. facilities, I want to make sure we're aligned on the legal launch checklist. I give the final legal approval for the rollout conditions, and under our launch-approval policy, I can approve with conditions as long as every required safeguard is stated as a concrete pre-launch condition and can be completed before deployment. Legal approval is withheld only when a required safeguard cannot be implemented before deployment. The launch package needs to identify the affected employee population, consent or labor restrictions, vendor-data restrictions, and the specific document or implementation action for each applicable safeguard. I'm aware the vendor's standard proposal permits collection and processing of employee voice recordings for authentication, but I need to hear from all of you on the privacy, labor, and information-security fronts before I can sign off. What do we know so far?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical gap. I reviewed the current employee roster and state-law matrix this week and confirmed that exactly 620 Illinois employees will be enrolled in this system. Illinois biometric law (BIPA) requires written opt-in consent before collecting their voiceprints and also requires the company to publish a retention schedule. These two points are not currently in the rollout approval memo. Both can be completed before deployment, but they must be added as concrete pre-launch conditions for me to sign off on the privacy front.
